newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close sharply up on recovery outlook.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close sharply up on recovery outlook.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Thursday, recovering more than half of Wednesday's losses on strong bargain-hunting triggered by recent bullish signs of a gathering recovery, brokers said.
The weighted index broke out of an early-session slump to close 101.58 points or 1.31 percent higher at 7,832.07.
Turnover was a relatively strong T$117.07 billion.

The market had tumbled 1.99 percent on Wednesday after the government rejected a planned T$800 million over-the-counter rights issue by Capital Securities, leading to speculation that the government was moving to cool the red-hot bourse.
The Securities and Exchange Commission countered before Thursday's market open that the rejection was an isolated case and did not signal a wider effort to dampen the market.
"The government's assurance encouraged investors to jump back into the market, reflecting a strong outlook for the economy," said Eric Liu, an analyst at National Securities.
The index has gained more than 1,000 points in 1997 as improving fourth-quarter and January economic indicators have spurred hopes that a still-sluggish recovery was accelerating.
Electronics shares, drubbed by profit-taking on Wednesday despite sound fundamentals, soared 3.14 percent on Thursday.
Motherboard giant Asustek, which listed in November at an underwriting price of T$108, closed at T$497 on Thursday after jumping the daily seven percent limit or T$32.
Brokers said investors largely ignored U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's overnight warning that the U.S. central bank may need to raise rates in coming months.
"Taiwan's market right now is completely dominated by local factors due to the economy's strength," said National's Liu. "Investors are paying no attention to what happens in the U.S."
Brokers expected the index to ride its recent momentum to test a higher cap on Friday. A 7,850-8,000 range was seen.
